name: Thirty-Two Frames
label: Revelation
lede: Jay Palumbo quit Elliott after False Cathedrals and started a Kentucky hardcore band, then handed the tapes to Elliott's drummer to engineer. The result was one EP, out on two labels in 2002.

eras.title: Out of Elliott, into Kentucky hardcore
eras.text: Jay Palumbo left Elliott after False Cathedrals over creative differences and recruited from the Kentucky hardcore scene: Thommy Browne, who drummed in Endpoint and Enkindels, and Mount Washington guitarist Jim Dzurovcak of XinvictusX.

years.h: Palumbo leaves Elliott and picks up the mic
years.p: Guitarist Jay Palumbo quits [[Elliott|b3250fd8-d202-4d4a-8fb3-1fdf88176aff]] after False Cathedrals over creative differences. In Thirty-Two Frames he sings as well as plays.
years.xp: Wikipedia's Elliott entry says Palumbo left after a tour with Hot Water Music, citing "personal reasons and creative differences with the rest of the band." False Cathedrals had come out on Revelation on August 22, 2000. No Echo's later feature describes the new band as starting as a "side-project" that turned into a "full-fledged rocking machine."

years.cap: Palumbo mid-song at left, a Thirty-Two Frames show, 2001-02
years.src: Discogs: Thirty-Two Frames (Rise Records 12") · Discogs: Jay Palumbo
years.h: Four months at NonLinear Studios, with Elliott's drummer at the board
years.p: Palumbo, Dzurovcak, bassist Jeremy Holehan and Browne produce themselves. [[Kevin Ratterman|44e97d75-ec33-42e8-907d-65fdea0f056d]], the drummer Palumbo left behind in Elliott, engineers with Mike Blaine.
years.xp: Discogs dates the sessions "May/September 2001" and credits the band as its own producer. Ratterman, Elliott's drummer, ended up recording the guitarist who walked out of his band.

eras.title: One session, two labels
eras.text: The same session came out twice in 2002: a six-song CD on Revelation and a longer vinyl on Rise Records, with a Tom Petty cover on the end.

years.src: No Echo · Discogs: Thirty-Two Frames (REV105 CD)
years.h: The self-titled EP lands on Revelation as REV105
years.p: Six songs, from the 1:53 opener Crow/Sioux War through Chippewa and Affluenza to Thanksgiving, which runs 8:28.
years.xp:
No Echo files the EP as Revelation's #105 and says it "failed to find its footing," calling it "little more than a footnote, as maligned as it is misunderstood." The same piece hears the band in the line of Dag Nasty, Strike Anywhere and Avail, with some Hot Water Music in the bass.

A fan-shot set from CBGB on November 2, 2002 survives on YouTube.

years.cap: The four-piece in a van doorway, 2002
years.src: Discogs: Thirty-Two Frames (Rise Records 12") · No Echo
years.h: Rise Records puts it on orange and black vinyl with a Tom Petty cover
years.p: The 12" (rise 022) adds ...And If I Said Nothing, Third Party Point of View and a cover of Petty's I Need To Know.
years.xp: Discogs lists the Rise pressing alongside the Revelation CD, a test pressing and a second colored-vinyl variant. The No Echo piece calls the Petty cover a secret track on the Revelation release.

eras.title: Back to the other bands
eras.text: Thirty-Two Frames left one record. The members went on in Kentucky bands, and in 2022 Palumbo was back on guitar in the one he'd walked out of.

years.h: Palumbo and Dzurovcak team up again in Sunday Evening Dinner Club
years.p: Palumbo also turns up in [[By the Grace of God|42a5a24f-7fa9-4790-879d-fe5fb3d91f9f]]. Browne keeps drumming in [[Black Cross|de4316a2-cd05-4bb6-9bc6-0c9290274a93]] and others.

years.h: Nineteen years on, Palumbo is back in Elliott for Furnace Fest
years.p: [[Elliott|b3250fd8-d202-4d4a-8fb3-1fdf88176aff]] broke up in 2003. For the 2022 reunion Palumbo plays guitar next to Chris Higdon and Ratterman.
years.xp: Brooklyn Vegan announced it as Elliott's first show in nearly 20 years, with Furnace Fest 2022 the only date on the table at the time. Wikipedia has the band disbanding in November 2003 after final European and US tours.
